what: A call of `should_not_reach()` runs to the end: `check_pass` of `fn should_not_reach() { _ }\nfn main() { should_not_reach(); }` passes (run 2026-11-12 on 136432aa02 plus this lane). MIR lowering turns `Expr::Underscore` into nothing (mir/lower.rs, `Expr::Underscore => Ok(Some(current))`), and the typed hole that inference reports does not stop the lowering. 251 calls in the MIR evaluator tests use it as their only assertion, so a wrong drop count or value in them is not caught.
cost: my first 30 runtime checks of drop order and layout all passed, the 2021 and 2024 editions with opposite expectations among them; found only because the file has a control (`the_oracle_catches_a_check_that_does_not_hold`)
cause: class: vacuous success. The helper was written when a typed hole failed MIR lowering (rust-analyzer); blaze lowers it since, and nothing checked the helper itself
state: fixed 2026-11-12: MIR lowering refuses a typed hole (`Expr::Underscore` is a TypeError), so the 251 calls assert again; two tests they hid were wrong themselves (drop_struct_field expected the old wrong count 2 for 3; the long list's fixture Box had no Drop impl, so nothing of it was dropped or counted), no front-end bug; and crates/hir-ty-mir/src/tests/assertion_helpers.rs holds every fixture's helper before its program runs (a `should_not_..` must not return when called, a `check`/`assert..` must have a call of type `!`), with its control
